title: How Long Does Paint Take to Dry Between Coats?
description: How long paint takes to dry between coats by type and brand, with recoat times, cure times, and what to do in cold or humid rooms.

cover.alt: Illustration of a clock on a painting blueprint background with a measuring tape

keywords: how long between coats of paint
takeaways: Most interior latex paint is dry to touch in 1 hour and ready to recoat in 2 to 4 hours at 77 F and 50 percent humidity.
Oil based paint needs 6 to 8 hours to dry to touch and a full 24 hours before you recoat it.
Dry is not cured. Latex paint takes 2 to 3 weeks to cure, so go easy on new walls until then.
body:
For most interior latex paint, wait 2 to 4 hours between coats. The paint feels dry to touch in about 1 hour, but recoat time is longer. Oil based paint is different. Wait 24 hours between coats. Those times assume 77 F (25 C) and 50 percent humidity, the test conditions on the can.

## Dry, recoat, and cure are three different times

- **Dry to touch:** the surface feels dry and will not leave paint on a clean fingertip. Dust will not stick much after this point.
- **Recoat time:** the first coat is firm enough to take a second coat without lifting, wrinkling, or going soft.
- **Cure time:** the paint has reached full hardness. Only then should you scrub it, hang heavy items tight to it, or let furniture press on it.

Sherwin-Williams puts latex cure at 2 to 3 weeks and oil based dry time at 6 to 8 hours. Behr says its Premium Plus film can be cleaned after 2 weeks. Read your can first.

| Paint type | Dry to touch | Wait before recoat | Full cure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Interior latex, Behr Premium Plus | 1 hour | 2 hours | 2 weeks |
| Interior latex, Sherwin-Williams SuperPaint | 1 hour | 4 hours | 2 to 3 weeks |
| Exterior latex, Sherwin-Williams Duration | 1 hour at 45 F and above | 4 hours at 45 F and above, 24 to 48 hours at 35 to 45 F | 2 to 3 weeks |
| Oil based or alkyd enamel | 6 to 8 hours | 24 hours | 5 to 15 days |

Behr Premium Plus shows 1 hour dry and 2 hour recoat on its product page. SuperPaint Interior lists 1 hour to touch and 4 hours to recoat. Same paint family, different rule. That is why brand matters.

If you are still picking paint and coats, our guide on [how many coats of paint you need](/blog/how-many-coats-of-paint/) helps you plan the full job before you open a can.

## Worked example: a 12 x 12 ft bedroom in one day

Say you paint a 12 x 12 ft (3.7 x 3.7 m) bedroom, walls only, two coats of Sherwin-Williams SuperPaint Interior. You start at 9:00 am.

Step 1, first coat time. Cut in the corners and edges first, then roll while the edges are still wet. For a room this size, allow 1.5 hours. First coat done at 10:30 am.

Step 2, recoat wait. SuperPaint lists 4 hours to recoat.

10:30 am + 4 hours = 2:30 pm. That is the earliest start for coat two.

Step 3, second coat time. Allow another 1.5 hours. Second coat done at 4:00 pm.

Step 4, check the total.

1.5 hours + 4 hours + 1.5 hours = 7 hours. 9:00 am + 7 hours = 4:00 pm. The math matches both ways.

Now swap the paint. With Behr Premium Plus at a 2 hour recoat, the total is 1.5 + 2 + 1.5 = 5 hours, done at 2:00 pm. Same room, same work, two hours saved. If the room were primed first, add the primer wait too. Our [primer calculator](/blog/primer-calculator/) covers how much primer a room like this takes.

Round your plan up, not down. If humidity is high or the room is cool, add an hour to the wait and check the wall before you roll.

## What makes paint dry slower or faster?

Temperature comes first. Cold paint dries slow. Sherwin-Williams Duration Exterior shows the point well. At 45 F and above, recoat is 4 hours. At 35 to 45 F, recoat jumps to 24 to 48 hours. A cool day can turn a one day job into a two day job.

Humidity comes next. Wet air slows water leaving the paint film. At 80 percent humidity, a latex coat that should recoat in 4 hours may still feel soft at 5 hours. Run a fan across the room, not straight at the wall. Open a window if the outside air is drier.

Film thickness matters too. A thick coat skins over and stays soft below. Two thin coats dry faster and look better. Dark colors can need extra time, and Behr notes cooler temperatures or higher humidity will prolong drying time. Paint on a glossy old coat also needs the full wait.

## How can you tell the first coat is ready?

Do not trust the clock alone. Use three checks together.

First, look. Wet paint has a shine. As it dries, the shine evens out. A patch that still looks darker or glossier than the rest is still wet.

Second, touch a hidden spot, low near the baseboard or behind where furniture will sit. It should feel dry, cool but not cold, and not tacky. If your fingertip drags or leaves a print, wait 30 minutes and test again.

Third, check the time on the can for your exact product. If the clock says ready but the touch test says tacky, the touch test wins. Conditions in your room beat lab conditions every time.

## What happens if you recoat too soon?

The second coat can lift and wrinkle the first. You may see streaks, soft spots, and a rough texture that will not roll out. Trapped water can also cause blisters days later and weak adhesion months later.

Fixing it costs more time than waiting. Let it dry hard, sand rough areas smooth, wipe off dust, and repaint. Prime any spots that peel to the old surface.

Waiting too long is less of a problem indoors. Most latex paints can be recoated days later with no prep beyond a dust wipe. Outside, or with enamel on cabinets and trim, a long gap can mean a light scuff sand helps the next coat grip. Check the can for a maximum recoat note.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I recoat latex paint after 1 hour if it feels dry?
No, not for most paints. Dry to touch at 1 hour is not the same as ready to recoat. Behr Premium Plus lists 2 hours to recoat, and Sherwin-Williams SuperPaint lists 4 hours. Use the recoat time on your can.

### How long does oil based paint take to dry between coats?
Plan on 24 hours. Oil based paint is dry to touch in 6 to 8 hours, per Sherwin-Williams, but the film is still soft. A second coat before 24 hours can wrinkle and stay soft for days.

### Does a fan make paint dry faster between coats?
A fan helps a little by moving moist air away from the wall. It does not cut a 4 hour recoat to 1 hour. Keep airflow gentle and steady, and do not point a heater at wet paint. Heat can skin the surface and trap moisture below.

### How long before I can put furniture back against a painted wall?
Wait at least 24 hours for light items that do not touch the wall. For bookcases, headboards, or anything that presses on the paint, wait a week or more. Full cure takes 2 to 3 weeks for latex, and paint can stick or dent until then.

### What if the room is cold or humid?
Add time. In a cool basement or a humid bathroom, add 1 to 2 hours to the listed recoat time and do the touch test before you roll. Below 50 F (10 C), most interior paints should not be applied at all. Behr lists 50 to 90 F (10 to 32 C) as its application range for Premium Plus.

### How long does primer need before paint?
Most latex primers recoat or take topcoat in 1 to 2 hours, but stain blocking and oil primers need longer. Read the primer can, and use the [paint calculator](/blog/paint-calculator/) to plan paint amounts once the primer coat is on your schedule.
